diagnosis_submitted: Probably a fracture of the wrist
summary: You asked how the injury happened. However, you did not ask when the injury happened or when the pain started. Partly correct. A fracture is likely, but the specific concern here is the scaphoid: fall on an outstretched hand plus anatomical snuffbox tenderness. Some of your notes are not supported by what was actually asked or examined.

diagnostic_assessment.explanation: Partly correct. A fracture is likely, but the specific concern here is the scaphoid: fall on an outstretched hand plus anatomical snuffbox tenderness.

next_steps: Complete the wrist examination: scaphoid tubercle tenderness and pain on axial thumb compression.
Request dedicated scaphoid-view radiographs; an initial X-ray can be normal.
If clinical suspicion remains despite normal X-rays: immobilise in a thumb spica splint and arrange repeat imaging or MRI.
Explain the plan and the risk of a missed scaphoid fracture (non-union, avascular necrosis) to the patient.
